messages.text: Need a second set of eyes on an underwriting exception for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0064}}. Renewal on the operating line, DSCR came back at 1.12x against our 1.25x policy floor. Anyone free to look at it this afternoon?
I can take it. What's driving the DSCR miss, one-time item or a structural drop in cash flow?
Mostly a one-time equipment repair plus a slow Q2 on receivables. Client says Q3 is already recovering. Loan is a_00137 if you want to pull the history in LoanOrigination.
FYI I'm rerunning the spreads for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0064}} with the repair add-back normalized. Should have the adjusted DSCR in about 20 min.
Careful with the add-back, policy only allows non-recurring items with third-party documentation. Do we have the invoice from the repair vendor in the file?
Good catch. Invoice is in DocVault but the proof of payment isn't. Brendan, can you get a bank statement showing it cleared?
Will ask the client now. Statements for the operating account should be quick, they usually respond same day.
Reminder that any exception over 10 bps of pricing relief or below DSCR floor needs a written mitigant and sign-off from two underwriters. Not just a verbal OK in the channel.
Understood. Tammy, would you be my second signer on this one? You're free of any relationship conflict since Brendan owns the client.
Yes, send me the memo once the adjusted numbers are in. I want to see the trailing 12 month cash flow and the covenant package.
Adjusted DSCR with normalized add-back comes to 1.24x. Still a hair under 1.25x, but close. Spreads are attached in the credit file.
That looks right to me. I'd suggest we also tighten the covenant to quarterly testing as a mitigant, plus a springing cash dominion if it dips below 1.15x.
Quarterly testing works for me. Cash dominion might be heavy for a client at medium risk with a clean payment history. Let's propose quarterly testing and a reporting trigger instead.

Unrelated but similar: {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0219}} consumer loan, a_00453, has a thin file on income docs. Can one of the seniors confirm whether the pay stub plus bank history satisfies the alt-doc exception?
Yes if you have 90 days of deposits that match the stub cadence. Document the reconciliation in the exception log. Happy to review it after I finish the memo for Brendan's deal.
Update: client sent the cleared payment proof for the repair. Uploaded to DocVault and linked it to the credit file. Joshua, you should be unblocked.
Thanks. Memo drafted with quarterly testing and a reporting trigger. Tammy, it's in your queue for the second signature. Once you sign it we can go back to the client with terms.
